subject: Literature
title: Myth in African American Literature
description: One-minute skill: Myth in African American Literature.

hook.text: Toni Morrison wove African mythology into her novels to rebuild cultural memory severed by the slave trade.

buildup.text: Song of Solomon features a man who learns he descends from Africans who could fly back to their homeland.

discovery.text: The flying African myth appears across the American South, passed down through generations of oral tradition.

twist.text: Morrison used myth not as escapism but as a tool for reclaiming the history that slavery tried to erase.

climax.text: Her work proved that mythology can be a form of resistance, rebuilding identity for displaced communities.

punchline.text: A myth about flying was really about going home.

quiz.question: How did Toni Morrison use mythology in her fiction?
options: She retold Greek myths in American settings
She used African mythology to rebuild cultural memory severed by slavery
She created entirely new mythologies with no historical basis
